prompts:
Create ONE coherent animation sprite sheet of the exact game character in the reference. The character identity, anatomy and tiny crisp PixelLab pixel clusters are locked by this reference. Use a strict 6-column by 4-row grid: 24 equal square transparent cells, read left-to-right then top-to-bottom. The same slim young male dark navy-haired swordsman with dark green ivory-edged short cape, oval silver breastplate, brown leather straps/gloves/boots, dark slim trousers and ONE plain straight silver sword. No new costume, no gold collar button, no different hairstyle.

Cells 1-4: four subtle FRONT-FACING IDLE breathing poses, sword held down beside right hand, matching the reference exactly.
Cells 5-12: EIGHT smooth FRONT-FACING WALK/RUN cycle poses, feet really alternate toe-off, passing and contact, small gentle stride, natural modest arm swing holding the sword securely, cape follows. Torso/head stay same camera scale and keep their crisp detail.
Cells 13-24: TWELVE smooth FRONT-FACING SWORD ATTACK poses: exact idle, join the grip with second hand, lift sword toward shoulder, both hands raise above crown, anticipation, blade behind head, decisive down-forward diagonal slash, low follow-through, settle, recover grip, return, exact idle. Not aimless arm waving. No effects or motion trails. Fingers clasp the hilt, connected natural elbows.

THIS IS ONE MODEL THROUGHOUT ALL ACTIONS. Same head width, face size, shoulder width, torso length, waist, leg length, boot thickness, palette and detail density in every cell. Native crown-to-sole height is 75 pixels, hair silhouette about 23 pixels wide and 16 tall. Every figure must have EXACTLY the same physical scale. A raised weapon must not make the body larger. A bent knee lowers the crown naturally by 1-3 logical pixels only. No broad/chubby attack body. No zoom or extra surface texture on moving poses. SAME tiny single-pixel highlights, sharp angular dark-blue hair spikes and stepped pixel contours across standing, walking and attacking.

Render all 24 cells as genuine low-resolution pixel game animation art at a logical 144x144 pixel cell, then nearest-neighbor enlargement of the whole sheet. Do not turn this into a smooth high-resolution illustration, chibi caricature, soft shaded figurine or noisy texture. Sharp opaque pixel edges, no blur, no antialiasing, no glow, no gradients, no ground shadow or background, no text, captions or grid lines. Transparent PNG. Hair, head, neck, body, clothes and sword are all painted continuously as ONE complete character per pose. The first idle and moving frames should look like the same exact sprite, only the pose changes.

Edit this exact 24-cell animation sprite sheet. Remove the entire dark blurred background completely, leaving real transparent alpha everywhere outside the characters, sword and cape. No shadows, no haze, no glow, no matte fringe. Preserve the precise 6-column 4-row arrangement, character positions, feet positions, poses, sprite edges and crisp pixel texture.

Also reduce every full head (hair, face and skull together, centered on its original neck) by about 12 percent in width and 8 percent in height, consistently across ALL twenty-four cells. The reference is a slim young adult, so hair silhouette width should be about 30 percent of full crown-to-sole body height, never wider. Keep all body, arm, leg, clothing and sword sizes unchanged. No new costume or hair design. Same head dimensions, same pixel detail density and same body proportions in standing, walking and attack cells. Especially do not make moving characters larger or fuzzier. Crisp native pixel art, opaque sharp edges, no resampling blur, no extra texture or text. Output transparent PNG.
